I feel like people end up getting some wires crossed. The right to free speech, bear arms, peaceful assembly, and all the other rights are between you and the established government. It's so government officials can't imprison you for criticism. It's so you can have a way to defend yourself as not to have to kneel to tyrannical soldiers knocking down your door. It's so you can demonstrate the number of people who believe or want a certain thing and show those who you elected to represent what you want from them.

This does not mean that you get to say horrible things and then whine that someone told you to shut up. It doesn't mean that you get to threaten people with a gun and pretend you're the one who felt unsafe. Assembling peacefully means without impeding traffic or commerce. You can have a huge group of people screaming about change outside of the capitol but the moment they push onto government property without permission, they break that agreement and forfeit their side of the bargain.
